events.title: Julius Caesar Assassinated on the Ides of March
events.description: Roman dictator Julius Caesar was stabbed to death by a group of senators, among them Marcus Junius Brutus and Decimus Junius Brutus. The attack happened at a meeting of the Senate in Rome.
events.significance: Caesar's murder did not save the Roman Republic. It set off a new round of civil wars and led to the rise of Augustus and the Roman Empire. The 'Ides of March' has been a byword for betrayal ever since.

events.title: Columbus Returns to Spain
events.description: Christopher Columbus arrived back in Spain after his first voyage across the Atlantic. He brought news of lands that were unknown to Europe.
events.significance: His return announced the voyage to Europe and opened the way to sustained contact, colonization and exchange between Europe and the Americas, with lasting consequences for both sides.

events.title: Maine Becomes the 23rd U.S. State
events.description: Maine was admitted to the Union as the twenty-third state. It separated from Massachusetts as part of the Missouri Compromise.
events.significance: Maine entered as a free state, which balanced the admission of slave-holding Missouri. The compromise delayed a national crisis over slavery for a generation.

events.title: Tsar Nicholas II Abdicates
events.description: Under pressure from the Russian Revolution, Nicholas II gave up the throne for himself and for his son. He named his brother as successor, but the brother declined the crown.
events.significance: The abdication ended more than 300 years of Romanov rule and the Russian monarchy. It cleared the way for the Provisional Government and, later that year, the Bolshevik seizure of power.

events.title: Germany Occupies Czechoslovakia
events.description: German troops marched into the remaining Czech lands of Bohemia and Moravia. Czechoslovakia ceased to exist as an independent state.
events.significance: The occupation broke the promises Hitler made at Munich in 1938 and ended the policy of appeasement. It pushed Britain and France toward confronting Germany, and World War II began less than six months later.
